title: Antonelli vs Russell: Career Wins Head-to-Head Explained
description: Kimi Antonelli now leads George Russell on career grand prix wins. The numbers, the theories behind Russell's slump, and how to track it with code.
author: freellm.site
content:
Kimi Antonelli has passed his Mercedes team-mate George Russell on career grand prix wins, after taking pole and winning the 2026 United States Grand Prix. Antonelli is in his second full season. Russell has been on the grid since 2019 and a Mercedes race driver since 2022, which is why the stat blew up on r/formula1 with 11,000+ upvotes instead of passing as a routine update.

![Antonelli vs Russell: Career Wins Head-to-Head Explained](/images/blog/antonelli-russell-career-wins-head-to-head/image-0.jpg)

This post does two things. It sets out what the head-to-head numbers say, as opposed to what the comment section assumed. And since this is a site about LLM APIs, not a motorsport blog, it shows how to automate what half that thread was doing by hand: a reproducible script that pulls the discussion, classifies the theories people propose, and counts them, using a free LLM API.

## What the head-to-head says

The original item came from The Race and is deliberately narrow: one counting stat, career grand prix wins, now tipped in Antonelli's favour. The thread quickly piled on related numbers, so it's worth separating what was reported from what was guesswork.

| Metric | Antonelli | Russell | Source quality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Career grand prix wins | Now ahead | Now behind | Reported (The Race) |
| Podiums since becoming team-mates in 2025 | 18 | 17 | Reported in a separate r/formula1 post |
| 2026 United States GP qualifying | Pole | P7 | Reported |
| 2026 United States GP result | Win | ~50s behind | Reported |
| 2026 championship position | Title contender | Community estimate: P5 to P6 | Projection, not official |

Two caveats. The podium count (18 vs 17) is a *since-2025* number covering only the period they've been team-mates, which is the fair comparison and also the harsher one for Russell. And the "Russell finishes fifth in a two-horse championship" line that drew hundreds of upvotes is a projection from commenters doing arithmetic on the remaining rounds, not a published standing. One reply put Lando Norris 31 points back and argued Russell could still slide to P6. For live, authoritative figures, use the [official F1 standings](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/drivers) rather than any aggregation, including this one.

One more stat: the thread's second-most-upvoted factual reply pointed out that Antonelli is now level with Charles Leclerc on career wins. That comparison says more than the Russell one, because Leclerc has been winning races since 2019.

## The four explanations people offered, and which hold up

The top comment was sympathy rather than analysis: what a nightmare, to finally get a championship-capable Mercedes and have it go like this. The follow-up, "what has actually happened to Russell?", got 1,700+ upvotes and produced four distinct theories.

### 1. He hasn't adapted to the 2026 regulations

The highest-rated explanation was that he has failed to adapt to this year's cars, and that an unsympathetic team environment has eroded his confidence on top of that. It's the most defensible claim in the thread because telemetry and qualifying deltas can test it, unlike claims about mood. Several commenters noted Russell lost his pace after sector one in US GP qualifying. A sector-specific gap, rather than general slowness, is what you'd expect from a driver fighting the car's balance in one type of corner.

### 2. Mentality collapse after reliability losses

Many commenters agreed on this one: Russell was publicly tipped as a title contender, then suffered reliability failures while his 19-year-old team-mate outpaced him. The people arguing it were careful about cause and effect, saying bad luck "masked" some genuinely poor performances rather than explaining all of them. That's the honest version. The weaker version, repeated often, treats every gap as psychological, which can't be tested.

### 3. The Bottas comparison

The most repeated framing was "Bottas 2.0," with some schadenfreude about Russell having criticised Bottas years ago. The best reply in the thread dismantled it. Bottas joined Mercedes in a dominant era and Russell arrived during the ground-effect struggle, so the situations aren't comparable, and the one time they had broadly equal machinery, Russell had the measure of him until a pit error. It's the clearest case in the discussion of a satisfying story beating an accurate one.

### 4. The Ricciardo comparison

A 764-upvote comment drew a longer parallel: an academy driver waits for a break, spends years at the back, finally gets the top seat next to a multiple champion and convincingly beats him, then the car isn't good enough and the next phase goes badly. This analogy holds up better than the Bottas one, and it's the closest the thread gets to a prediction rather than a joke.

None of the top comments separated *qualifying* pace from *race* pace or adjusted for grid position before comparing finishing gaps. Finishing 50 seconds behind a pole-sitter from P7 is a different claim from a 50-second deficit starting on the same row. To argue about this properly, you need that split.

## Why an AI site is writing about this

First, the Mercedes garage already produced one AI-related story this season: [Kimi's New Race Engineer 'Giorgio' Was George Russell](/blog/kimi-antonelli-russell-radio-prank-ai/) covers the radio prank that convinced a lot of people a synthetic voice was involved.

Second, a 668-comment thread is a dataset. Reading it by hand to see which explanation dominates is the kind of job LLM classification does well, and you can do it on a free tier without a credit card.

## Build the thread classifier

Here's a runnable script. It takes comments, asks a model to put each one into a fixed set of explanation buckets, and tallies the result. It uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint pattern, so you can point `base_url` at any free provider; see [OpenAI-Compatible Free LLM APIs: The Drop-In List](/blog/openai-compatible-free-llm-apis-list/) for current options, and [What Is an OpenAI-Compatible API](/blog/openai-compatible-api-guide/) if the pattern is new to you.

```python
import os, json, collections
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["LLM_API_KEY"],
    base_url=os.environ["LLM_BASE_URL"],  # your free provider's OpenAI-compatible URL
)
MODEL = os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL", "llama-3.3-70b-versatile")

BUCKETS = [
    "car_adaptation",      # can't get on top of the new regs
    "mentality",           # confidence / psychological
    "reliability_luck",    # DNFs, strategy, bad luck
    "teammate_is_elite",   # Antonelli is just that good
    "team_environment",    # garage not supporting him
    "joke_or_meme",        # Bottas 2.0, humiliation ritual, etc.
    "other",
]

SYSTEM = (
    "You label forum comments about an F1 driver's poor form. "
    f"Return strict JSON: {{\"bucket\": one of {BUCKETS}, \"confidence\": 0-1}}. "
    "Pick the single dominant claim. Comments that are only jokes go to joke_or_meme."
)

def classify(comment: str) -> dict:
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL,
        temperature=0,
        response_format={"type": "json_object"},
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": comment[:2000]},
        ],
    )
    return json.loads(resp.choices[0].message.content)

comments = [
    "He never adapted to this year's car and the team hasn't helped him.",
    "Bottas 2.0 incoming",
    "Forecast a title, then three DNFs. Anyone's head would go.",
    "Kimi is simply a generational talent, this isn't on George.",
]

counts = collections.Counter()
for c in comments:
    out = classify(c)
    if out.get("confidence", 0) >= 0.5:
        counts[out["bucket"]] += 1
    print(f"{out['bucket']:<18} {c[:60]}")

print("\nTally:", counts.most_common())
```

Four practical notes from running this kind of job on free tiers:

- **Set `temperature=0`.** Classification isn't a creative task, and labels that drift between runs make your tally meaningless.
- **Keep the bucket list closed and include `other`.** Without an escape hatch, the model forces comments into the wrong buckets and inflates your top category.
- **Batch under the rate limit.** Hundreds of comments will hit per-minute caps on most free plans. Compare them in [Free LLM API Rate Limits Compared](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/) and add a sleep or a concurrency cap.
- **Spot-check 20 labels by hand** before you trust the totals. For the full pipeline with scoring and thresholds, [Sentiment Analysis With a Free LLM API in Python](/blog/sentiment-analysis-free-llm-api-python/) covers it end to end.

For a high-volume job that needs little reasoning, like this one, a fast small model beats a frontier model on both cost and latency. [Best Free LLM APIs in 2026](/blog/best-free-llm-apis-2026/) lists what's currently available without a card.

## The caveat

A classifier tells you what a forum *believes*, weighted by upvotes. It doesn't tell you why a driver is slow. The most-upvoted explanation in that thread, regulation adaptation plus a cold garage, is plausible and partly checkable; the Bottas framing is popular and mostly wrong. An LLM counting comments won't tell those apart for you. Use the tool to measure the conversation, then go to sector times and official results to measure the car.

## FAQ

### Does Antonelli have more career wins than Russell now?

Yes. That's the specific claim The Race reported and the reason the thread exists. The same discussion noted that Antonelli is also level with Charles Leclerc on career wins. For current exact totals, check the official F1 results pages rather than a secondary summary.

### What is Antonelli's podium record against Russell?

Since the pair became Mercedes team-mates in 2025, a separate r/formula1 post put Antonelli on 18 podiums to Russell's 17. That window is the right comparison because it only covers races in the same machinery.

### Is Russell going to finish fifth in the championship?

Commenters projected P5, and some argued P6 was possible with Norris 31 points back. These are fan projections, not official standings, so check formula1.com before repeating them.

### Can I run the classifier in this post for free?

Yes, if your provider's free tier covers chat completions and JSON mode. On a 600-comment thread, rate limits are the real constraint, not cost, so see the rate-limit comparison linked above and throttle accordingly.

### Which model should I use for comment classification?

A small fast instruct model with JSON-mode support is usually enough. Save larger models for labels that need reasoning across the whole thread. JSON-mode support varies between providers more than raw capability does, so check each provider's docs.
